slide.title: Four Images, One Look
slide.body: Four generated product images in a row on pale peach: serum bottle, cream jar, toner bottle, lip balm tube, no brand marks. Small tag: AI Image Generation · Lesson 6.

scenes.voiceover: One good AI image is easy. Four images that look like they come from the same photo shoot are much harder. Every new generation starts from new random noise, so things drift. Today, you get the tools to keep a set together.

slide.title: Keeping Images Consistent
slide.body: AI Image Generation and Visual Design · Lesson 6 of 12 · Screen demo. Four generated images drifting apart: light direction, palette and background change.

scenes.voiceover: Style drift is when images that should belong together slowly become different. The light changes direction, the palette shifts, or the background moves from a studio to a kitchen. There are four main ways to control it.

slide.title: 1 A fixed style block
slide.body: Four prompt cards. Top line of each is a different subject; the bottom paragraph, the style block, is identical and highlighted in teal on all four.

scenes.voiceover: The first and most important is a fixed style block. This is a paragraph that describes style, lighting, colour and framing. You paste it, word for word, into every prompt in the set. Only the subject line changes. It works in every tool.

slide.title: 2 Reference image · 3 Reference settings
slide.body: Reference image: attach your best result and say what to keep (Gemini) · Style reference: an image guides the look (Firefly) · Structure reference: an image guides layout and shapes (Firefly)

scenes.voiceover: The second is a reference image. You upload an image, often your best result so far, and ask the tool to match its look. In Gemini, you can attach an image to your message and describe what to keep. The third is Firefly's reference settings, where an image guides the style, or the layout and shapes.

slide.title: 4 Seeds
slide.body: Reuse a seed with a similar prompt: a similar starting point · Many consumer tools hide seeds · Do not depend on this method

scenes.voiceover: The fourth is the seed. Where a tool lets you see and reuse a seed, it can keep a similar starting point. But many consumer tools hide seeds, so do not depend on this method.

scenes.stock_query: amateur sports team in matching uniforms
scenes.voiceover: A style block is like a uniform for a sports team. Each player is different, but the same colours and badge make everyone look like one team. The reference image is the photo of the uniform you show to a new player.

scenes.on_screen_text: Upload only images you may use
scenes.voiceover: One safety note. Upload only images you own or have permission to use as references. No client files, and no photos of people without consent.

slide.title: Min-seo's style block
slide.body:
Style block: product photograph on a seamless pale peach background,
single soft light from the upper left with a gentle shadow to the lower right,
close-up at eye level, product centred with generous empty space around it,
limited palette of pale peach, white and soft sage green,
calm, clean and fresh mood

scenes.voiceover: Let's help Min-seo. She runs a skincare start-up in Seoul, South Korea, and needs four product images for her website. Her style block is on screen. A pale peach background, one soft light from the upper left, a close-up at eye level, a peach, white and sage green palette, and a calm, clean mood.

screen_steps: Open Gemini and start a new chat
Paste: 'A frosted glass serum bottle with a white dropper.'
Paste the style block below it and press send
Download the best result: this is the hero image
scenes.voiceover: I open Gemini and start a new chat. I paste the first subject, a frosted glass serum bottle with a white dropper, then the style block, and send. I download the best result. This is our hero image.

screen_steps: In the same chat, use the attach or upload option to add the hero image
Type: 'Create a new image in exactly the same style, background and lighting as this reference. Subject: a white cream jar with a wooden lid.'
Paste the style block again and press send
scenes.voiceover: For the next image, I stay in the same chat and attach the hero image as a reference. I ask for a new image in exactly the same style, background and lighting, with a new subject, a white cream jar with a wooden lid. And I paste the style block again.

screen_steps: Repeat the reference request with 'a tall sage-green toner bottle'
Repeat again with 'a small tube of lip balm'
Download each result
scenes.voiceover: I repeat this for a tall sage green toner bottle, and a small tube of lip balm. Each time, only the subject changes.

screen_steps: Open Adobe Firefly and choose text to image
Paste the subject line and the style block
Find the style reference setting and upload the hero image
scenes.voiceover: Now the same idea in Adobe Firefly. I choose text to image and paste the subject line and the style block. Then I find the style reference setting and upload the hero image.

screen_steps: If a reference strength setting exists, adjust it and point out how the result changes
Click Generate
Repeat with the next subject, keeping the reference and style block the same
scenes.voiceover: If there is a strength control, I move it. Watch how a stronger reference pulls the result closer to the hero image. I generate, then repeat with the next subject, keeping the reference and the style block the same.

screen_steps: Place the 4 images in a row
Check background colour, light direction, shadow position and framing
Point to the lip balm image: its shadow is stronger than the others
scenes.on_screen_text: Check each image against the hero
scenes.voiceover: Finally, the review. I place the four images in a row and check the background colour, the light direction, the shadow position and the framing. The lip balm image has a stronger shadow than the others.

screen_steps: Add 'very soft, faint shadow' to the lip balm prompt only
Regenerate that image
Show the 4 images in a row again
scenes.voiceover: So I add very soft, faint shadow to that prompt only, and regenerate that one image.

The most common mistake is to rewrite the style block a little each time, like soft light for one image and gentle daylight for the next. Small word changes create visible drift. Copy and paste the block exactly, and check each new image as you go.

slide.title: Key takeaways
slide.body: 1. A fixed style block, word for word, in every prompt. 2. References help match the hero image. 3. Check each image against the hero; fix drift one at a time.

scenes.voiceover: Let's recap. First, a fixed style block, pasted word for word into every prompt, is the most reliable way to keep a set consistent. Second, reference images and reference settings help you match a chosen hero image. Third, check each new image against the hero for background, light, palette and framing, and fix drift one image at a time.
